responses:
## Assessment

All three prior attempts kept the same structure and produced the same cost (3567). Each one changed only comments or the shape of the length dispatch, so the instruction count didn't move. The likely cost drivers are the per-word `OnesCount64` work and the bounds checks on each `xs[i]` index, not the dispatch ladder. The ladder is only a few compares per call.

The change below targets the bounds checks in the hot 16-word block. Taking a fixed-length view `w := xs[:16]` lets every index in that block be checked against the constant length 16. Optimizing backends can then prove the checks redundant. The block still performs one `OnesCount64` per word and one recursive call. Whether giri's SSA benefits depends on whether it runs a prove-style pass, so the gain is uncertain. It is a small, safe change, and it does not alter the result or mutate `xs`.

## Expected effect

- Correctness is unchanged: the same 16 words are counted, and the recursion still receives `xs[16:]`.
- Cost may drop slightly on inputs of 16 or more words if the bounds checks are eliminated. If giri does not optimize, the cost will stay at about 3567. Either way, the function is not made worse.
- If this does not move the score, the next thing to try is a different per-word strategy. The intrinsic call count is the floor for the current approach.
